salt_short_builtmysteries_2026.apa: Built Mysteries. (2026, October 15). Utah built a railroad across a lake. Then the lake turned two different colors. [Video]. YouTube. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=A_2YCf9X4X0

shots.caption: Opening shot of the line on the causeway, and the map with the straight crossing
shots.quote: It's the Great Salt Lake, and a railroad runs straight across the middle of it.

shots.caption: The 1904 wooden bridge (about 12 mi) and the 1950s rock fill (about 20 mi)
shots.quote: At first, the tracks crossed on a wooden bridge almost 12 mi long ... In the 1950s, the railroad replaced it with a solid wall of rock and gravel, almost 20 mi long.

shots.caption: Four frames at the times of the spoken claims (straight across, 1904 route, 12 mi trestle, 20 mi fill)
shots.quote: In 1904, the Southern Pacific wanted a shortcut west, and instead of going around the lake, it went straight across.

salt_short_builtmysteries_2026.note: Words are from the automatic English captions (short.en.vtt). Channel Built Mysteries, uploaded 2026-10-15, 70 s.

salt_sp_1987.apa: Southern Pacific Transportation Company, Sacramento Division. (1987). [Letter of welcome, maps and elevation chart for American Railroad Engineering Association members attending the Fall Technical Conference, Great Salt Lake field trip] [Unpublished booklet, signed by J. W. Lynch, Superintendent, and J. J. Deis, Division Engineer]. Ogden, UT: Southern Pacific Transportation Company.

shots.caption: End points of the Lucin Cutoff by milepost
shots.quote: The Lucin Cutoff, between Lucin, Utah (MP 678.5) and Ogden, Utah (MP 781.1)

shots.caption: Length of the Cutoff, mileposts of the five parts of the lake crossing, length of the trestle
shots.quote: The new Cutoff was 102.6 miles long, at a cost of 8.4 million dollars. Originally, the Great Salt Lake crossing was as follows: 1. Rambo Fill, MP 735.2 (Lakeside) to MP 739.7 (Tresend). 2. Great Salt Lake Trestle, MP 739.7 (Tresend) to MP 752.2 (Bridge). Built to elevation of 4,217 feet above sea level (Hood's Datum). 3. Saline Fill, MP 752.2 (Bridge) to MP 753.6 (Saline). 4. Promontory Peninsula, MP 753.6 (Saline) to MP 759.0 (Promontory Point). 5. Bagley Fill, MP 759.0 (Promontory Point) to MP 766.62 (Little Mountain). ... The trestle, when completed, was to be twelve miles long, consisting of 28,250 piles, ranging from 100-150 feet in length.

shots.page: map, Sacramento Division sheet no. 2 (PDF p. 7)
shots.caption: Route map with milepost flags 678.5 (Lucin), 735.2 (Lakeside) and 781.1 (Ogden)

shots.page: chart 'Elevations of the Great Salt Lake', dated Sept. 29, 1987 (PDF p. 8)
shots.caption: Time line labels for the 1902 trestle and the 1959 causeway
shots.quote: LUCIN CUT-OFF AND 12-MILE TRESTLE CONSTRUCTED 1902 ... 12-MILE CAUSEWAY TO REPLACE TRESTLE BUILT 1959

salt_nrhp_1972.apa: U.S. National Park Service. (1972). Southern Pacific Railroad: Ogden-Lucin Cut-Off Trestle (National Register of Historic Places nomination, reference no. 72001257; file includes the 2018 removal request) [Nomination form]. U.S. Department of the Interior.

shots.caption: Lengths of temporary and permanent trestle and fill; length of the trestle in 1971
shots.quote: Approximately 12 miles of temporary trestle (four - 40 foot piles per bent) and 11 miles of permanent trestle (five - 70 foot piles per bent) were constructed in addition to the 10 miles of fill. ... The present 11.88 mile trestle consists of the original permanent structure in addition to the engle siding which is built over the temporary trestle piling. Today the trestle supplements the adjacent causeway (c. 1959) with overload and emergency rail traffic.

shots.caption: Route of the cut-off from Ogden across the lake to Lucin
shots.quote: The cut-off eliminated 44 miles of extreme grades and curves found on the original transcontinental route through the Promontory Mountains. The new route ran 20 miles west from Ogden to the Great Salt Lake, crossed the lake at Promontory Point, and continued for 50 miles over the Great Salt Desert to Lucin.
